title: THE OFFERING THAT COULD NOT BE EATEN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"Any male in a priest's family may eat it; it is most holy. But any sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place must not be eaten; it must be burned up."'" - Lev 6:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a distinction we met in chapter 4. Most sin offerings were eaten by the priests. But when the blood was carried inside the tent — as it was for the high priest's sin and for the whole community's — nothing could be eaten. It all burned outside the camp.

The most serious sins required the most complete removal. Nobody benefited. Nothing remained.

Hebrews takes this exact detail and builds on it: The high priest carries the blood of animals into the Most Holy Place as a sin offering, but the bodies are burned outside the camp. And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood (Heb 13:11-12).

Christ fulfilled the highest category. His blood went into the true sanctuary, not a copy (Heb 9:24). His body was taken outside the city. He was the sin offering that nobody could share in, that nobody could profit from, that was entirely consumed.

There is a finality here that should settle every believer. The greatest sin offering has already been made. It cannot be repeated, added to, or improved upon.

Leviticus 6 ends with fire. The gospel ends with a Saviour saying, "It is finished" (Jn 19:30).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I resting in a sacrifice that is complete, or still trying to contribute to it?
2. What would it mean to live today in the light of "It is finished"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You were the offering carried outside the camp, and Your work is finished. I rest in it entirely today. Amen.
